literal: He compiled ten juan of Exemplary Precedents for Publication, which circulated in his day; he also worked through the Mao version of the Odes in chapter-and-commentary form, and with these two classics instructed Prince of Qi'an, Kuo.
idiomatic: He compiled ten juan of Exemplary Precedents for Publication, which circulated in his day; he also worked through the Mao version of the Odes in chapter-and-commentary form, and with these two classics instructed Prince of Qi'an, Kuo.

literal: At the start of Wuping he was a doctor of the Imperial University.
idiomatic: At the opening of Wuping he was a doctor of the Imperial University.

literal: Zhang Diao was a man of Pingbei in Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Zhang Diao came from Pingbei in Zhongshan.

literal: His family had been poor and lowly, yet he was generous and possessed resolve; he loved antiquity and classical learning.
idiomatic: His house was poor and low, yet he was open-handed and full of resolve, with a deep love for antiquity and the old learning.

literal: His strength was beyond other men; he carried a book-chest and followed teachers, not shrinking from a thousand li.
idiomatic: His strength was beyond other men; he shouldered a book-chest and followed teachers a thousand li without flinching.

literal: He mastered the Five Classics throughout, and was especially clear in the Three Commentaries; students who came from afar to study under him numbered in the hundreds, and the ru scholars submitted to his force in debate.
idiomatic: He mastered the Five Classics throughout and was especially clear in the Three Commentaries; students who came from afar to study under him numbered in the hundreds, and the ru scholars bowed to his force in debate.

literal: At the end of Wei he was summoned into the hegemon's office on account of his mastery of the classics; Gaozu ordered him to lecture and read with the princes.
idiomatic: At the end of Wei he was summoned into the hegemon's office for his mastery of the classics; Gaozu ordered him to lecture and read with the princes.

literal: He began his career as General Who Extinguishes Bandits, and was gradually promoted to long-flow aide in the Grand Marshal's office and chief clerk of Ding province.
idiomatic: He began his career as General Who Extinguishes Bandits, then rose by degrees to long-flow aide in the Grand Marshal's office and chief clerk of Ding province.

literal: He followed Shizong to Bing and was made long-flow aide in the Prince of Changshan's establishment office.
idiomatic: He followed Shizong to Bing and was made long-flow aide in the Prince of Changshan's establishment office.

literal: In the Tianbao era he was a staff officer in the Prince of Yong'an's establishment office.
idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he served as staff officer in the Prince of Yong'an's establishment office.

literal: When Xianzu died at Jinyang, Diao was promoted to acting director in the Ministry of Rites and oversaw the mourning; he accompanied the bier back to Ye.
idiomatic: When Xianzu died at Jinyang, Diao was promoted to acting director in the Ministry of Rites to oversee the mourning and accompanied the bier back to Ye.

literal: At the start of Qianming he was made doctor of the Imperial University.
idiomatic: At the opening of Qianming he was made doctor of the Imperial University.

literal: He was moved to governor of Pingyuan and lost his post on a charge of bribery.
idiomatic: He was moved to governor of Pingyuan and lost his post on a charge of bribery.

literal: When Shizu took the throne, on account of old favor he was made attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.
idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, old favor won him the post of attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.

literal: Prince of Langye Yan sought a doctor steeped in Confucian learning; the authorities nominated Diao, and at the time people said the right man had been found.
idiomatic: Prince of Langye Yan wanted a doctor steeped in Confucian learning; the authorities nominated Diao, and the talk of the time said the right man had been found.

literal: Soon he was made inspector of Jing province.
idiomatic: Soon he was made inspector of Jing province.

literal: Before long he was appointed attendant of irregular cavalry and again lectured for Yan.
idiomatic: Before long he was appointed attendant of irregular cavalry and again lectured for Yan.

literal: It happened that Ma Jingde, the emperor's lecturer-in-attendance, died; Diao then entered to transmit the classics.
idiomatic: When Ma Jingde, the emperor's lecturer-in-attendance, died, Diao entered to transmit the classics in his place.

literal: The emperor valued him highly, made him a reader-in-attendance, and with Zhang Jingren he was alike honored; together they entered the Hall of Splendid Light to read the Spring and Autumn Annals.
idiomatic: The emperor valued him highly, made him reader-in-attendance, and with Zhang Jingren he shared equal honor; together they entered the Hall of Splendid Light to read the Spring and Autumn Annals.

literal: He was further made Director of the Imperial University, given acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall.
idiomatic: He was further made Director of the Imperial University, given acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall.

literal: The Hu man He Hongzhen had won the ruler's intimate favor; he and Zhang Jingren became kin by marriage.
idiomatic: The Hu man He Hongzhen had won the ruler's intimate favor; he and Zhang Jingren bound their houses by marriage.

literal: Because Jingren was of the imperial clan, Diao attached himself to Hongzhen and poured out his heart in courtesy; day by day their affection grew close, and in public and private affairs Diao often served as his guide.
idiomatic: Because Jingren was of the imperial clan, Diao attached himself to Hongzhen and poured out his heart in courtesy; day by day their affection grew close, and in public and private affairs Diao often served as his guide.

literal: At that time Mutipo, Han Changluan, and Hongzhen alike attended within the curtain; knowing Diao was Hongzhen's chief strategist, they deeply hated him.
idiomatic: At that time Mutipo, Han Changluan, and Hongzhen alike attended within the curtain; knowing Diao was Hongzhen's chief strategist, they hated him to the bone.

literal: Hongzhen also memorialized that Diao should supervise the national history.
idiomatic: Hongzhen also memorialized that Diao should supervise the national history.

literal: Soon he was made attendant-in-chief, given the grand marshal's office, and put in charge of revenue affairs; he was greatly entrusted, and his words were often followed.
idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant-in-chief, given the grand marshal's office, and put in charge of revenue affairs; he was greatly entrusted, and his words were often followed.

literal: A special edict allowed him to report without hurrying; he was called the Doctor.
idiomatic: A special edict allowed him to report without hurrying; the court called him the Doctor.

literal: Diao, knowing he had risen from the humblest origins to the rank of great minister, strove in public affairs with a spirit that would not spare his own body, wishing to establish merit and repay the court's grace.
idiomatic: Diao, knowing he had risen from the humblest origins to great minister, strove in public affairs with a spirit that would not spare his own body, wishing to establish merit and repay the court's grace.

literal: In debate he would raise or lower a point without evasion.
idiomatic: In debate he would raise or lower a point without evasion.

literal: Unnecessary expenses within the palace were sharply reduced; those about him who indulged in license were strictly restrained; he repeatedly rebuked the favored and powerful and offered counsel at the throne's side.
idiomatic: Unnecessary expenses within the palace were sharply cut; those about him who indulged in license were strictly restrained; he repeatedly rebuked the favored and powerful and offered counsel at the throne's side.

literal: The ruler also leaned on him deeply and was about to entrust him with court government.
idiomatic: The ruler also leaned on him deeply and was about to entrust him with the government of the court.

literal: Diao then took clarification as his own charge, and his spirit ran very high.
idiomatic: Diao then took clarification as his own charge, and his spirit ran very high.

literal: Once in the court hall he said to Zheng Zixin: "When I went into the Secretariat just now, I saw your esteemed family's Tang Ling's dispositions were utterly without reason. If it were making a few lines of military registers, Diao would not match Yong; if it were bringing the ruler to Yao and Shun and oneself occupying the stations of Hou Ji and Qi, then Yong would not match me."
idiomatic: Once in the court hall he said to Zheng Zixin, "When I went into the Secretariat just now, I saw your esteemed family's Tang Ling's dispositions were utterly without reason. If it were making a few lines of military registers, Diao would not match Yong; if it were bringing the ruler to Yao and Shun and oneself occupying the stations of Hou Ji and Qi, then Yong would not match me."

literal: His arrogance and extravagance were such as this.
idiomatic: His arrogance and extravagance ran to such a pitch.

literal: Changluan and the rest feared he would not cease meddling in government and secretly plotted against him.
idiomatic: Changluan and the rest feared he would not cease meddling in government and plotted against him in secret.

literal: It happened that Diao, together with the attendant-in-chief Cui Jishu and others, remonstrated against the emperor's journey to Jinyang; Changluan therefore slandered them, and so all were put to death.
idiomatic: It happened that Diao, together with attendant-in-chief Cui Jishu and others, remonstrated against the emperor's journey to Jinyang; Changluan slandered them, and so all were put to death.

literal: At the execution the emperor ordered Duan Xiaoyan to question him.
idiomatic: At the execution the emperor ordered Duan Xiaoyan to question him.

literal: Diao replied: "Your servant rose from among the ru scholars, was wrongly drawn up and promoted, received office through successive reigns, and constantly enjoyed grace; I reached grand marshal's office and attendant-in-chief, with glory and favor heaped upon me.
idiomatic: Diao replied, "Your servant rose from among the ru scholars, was wrongly drawn up and promoted, received office through successive reigns, and constantly enjoyed grace; I reached grand marshal's office and attendant-in-chief, with glory and favor heaped upon me.

literal: Each time I thought how dust and dew might in the smallest measure repay mountains and seas.
idiomatic: Each time I thought how dust and dew might in the smallest measure repay mountains and seas.

literal: In today's remonstrance I was truly the chief plotter; the intent was good but the outcome evil, and there is no escaping death.
idiomatic: In today's remonstrance I was truly the chief plotter; the intent was good but the outcome evil, and there is no escaping death.

literal: I humbly pray Your Majesty will treasure gold and jade, open and develop your divine clarity, often summon men of Jia Yi's sort to discuss the way of governance, so that between what you hear and behold nothing is blocked—and then though the day of my death come, it will be as a day of life."
idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty will treasure gold and jade, open and develop your divine clarity, often summon men of Jia Yi's sort to discuss the way of governance, so that between what you hear and behold nothing is blocked—and then though the day of my death come, it will be as a day of life."

literal: He sobbed with tears streaming, bowed his head and went to the blade; the guards on either side all pitied him and yet found him splendid.
idiomatic: He sobbed with tears streaming, bowed his head and went to the blade; the guards on either side all pitied him and yet found him splendid.

literal: He was fifty-five.
idiomatic: He was fifty-five.

literal: His son Dechong and the rest were banished to the northern frontier.
idiomatic: His son Dechong and the rest were banished to the northern frontier.

literal: When Nan'an rebelled, Dechong and his younger brother Dejie both died.
idiomatic: When Nan'an rebelled, Dechong and his younger brother Dejie both died.

literal: Dechong was harmonious, careful, and yielding, skilled in human relations, clever and fond of learning, and had dipped into letters and histories.
idiomatic: Dechong was harmonious, careful, and yielding, skilled in human relations, clever and fond of learning, and had dipped into letters and histories.

literal: As the son of the emperor's teacher, he was early singled out for promotion.
idiomatic: As the son of the emperor's teacher, he was early singled out for promotion.

literal: He passed through attendant of irregular cavalry outside the regular roster and recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment office, then entered as gentleman of the Secretariat and, by precedent, was kept on call.
idiomatic: He passed through attendant of irregular cavalry outside the regular roster and recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment office, then entered as gentleman of the Secretariat and, by precedent, was kept on call.

literal: At his father's execution Dechong was on duty in the palace hall; he saw the cruel injustice with his own eyes, wailed until he collapsed senseless on the ground, and only after long while came back to himself.
idiomatic: At his father's execution Dechong was on duty in the palace hall; he saw the cruel injustice with his own eyes, wailed until he collapsed senseless on the ground, and only after a long while came back to himself.

literal: Sun Linghui was a man of Wuqiang in Changle.
idiomatic: Sun Linghui came from Wuqiang in Changle.

literal: Huiwei, the great ru of Wei and director of the Secretariat, was Linghui's great-great-grandfather on his mother's side.
idiomatic: Huiwei, the great ru of Wei and director of the Secretariat, was Linghui's great-great-grandfather on his mother's side.

literal: Linghui from youth was bright and keen, with capacity and measure.
idiomatic: Linghui from youth was bright and keen, with capacity and measure.

literal: Huiwei's one son had died early; most of the family's books were there.
idiomatic: Huiwei's one son had died early; most of the family's books were there.

literal: At seven sui Linghui already loved learning; each day he recited several thousand words, seeking out only the chapter summaries Huiwei had copied by hand, and not asking teachers or friends.
idiomatic: At seven sui Linghui already loved learning; each day he recited several thousand words, seeking out only the chapter summaries Huiwei had copied by hand, and not asking teachers or friends.

literal: The Three Rites and the Three Commentaries he all mastered in their main purport; when he first went to Bao Jixiang and Xiong Ansheng to question what puzzled him, what he brought to light left Xiong and Bao with nothing to differ over.
idiomatic: The Three Rites and the Three Commentaries he mastered in their main purport; when he first went to Bao Jixiang and Xiong Ansheng to question what puzzled him, what he brought to light left Xiong and Bao with nothing to differ over.

literal: He was nominated as the Ji province's xiucai; in the archery-and-writing examination he took a high place and was given the rank of acting general outside the regular roster.
idiomatic: He was nominated as the Ji province's xiucai; in the archery-and-writing examination he took a high place and was given the rank of acting general outside the regular roster.

literal: Later, because his Confucian learning was clear and distinguished, he was promoted and appointed doctor of the Grand Academy.
idiomatic: Later, because his Confucian learning was clear and distinguished, he was promoted and appointed doctor of the Grand Academy.

literal: He was moved to supervisory aide of North Xuzhou and then transferred to governor of Tong commandery.
idiomatic: He was moved to supervisory aide of North Xuzhou and then transferred to governor of Tong commandery.

literal: In the Tiantong era an edict ordered court ministers to recommend who might serve as teacher to Prince of Nanyang, Chuo; the Minister of Personnel Yu Jin memorialized him; he was summoned as doctor of the Imperial University and transmitted the classics to the prince.
idiomatic: In the Tiantong era an edict ordered court ministers to recommend who might serve as teacher to Prince of Nanyang, Chuo; the Minister of Personnel Yu Jin memorialized him; he was summoned as doctor of the Imperial University and transmitted the classics to the prince.

literal: Though the prince did not love letters, he still greatly respected Linghui and memorialized to make him consulting aide in the prince's establishment office.
idiomatic: Though the prince did not love letters, he still greatly respected Linghui and memorialized to make him consulting aide in the prince's establishment office.

literal: When Chuo was made inspector of Ding province, Linghui still followed him to the garrison.
idiomatic: When Chuo was made inspector of Ding province, Linghui still followed him to the garrison.

literal: What Chuo did was reckless and violent; Linghui could only grieve in silence and could not remonstrate and stop him.
idiomatic: What Chuo did was reckless and violent; Linghui could only grieve in silence and could not remonstrate and stop him.

literal: Chuo wished to make his recorder Ma Zijie consulting aide; he therefore memorialized asking to transfer Linghui to prince's teacher and make Zijie consulting aide.
idiomatic: Chuo wished to make his recorder Ma Zijie consulting aide; he therefore memorialized asking to transfer Linghui to prince's teacher and make Zijie consulting aide.

literal: The court held that prince's teacher was third rank and that such a memorial did not accord with regulations.
idiomatic: The court held that prince's teacher was third rank and that such a memorial did not accord with regulations.

literal: The Later Ruler wrote a reply beneath the memorial: "Simply use him," and still wrote in his own hand to the Prince of Nanyang; both followed what had been memorialized.
idiomatic: The Later Ruler wrote a reply beneath the memorial: "Simply use him," and still wrote in his own hand to the Prince of Nanyang; both followed what had been memorialized.

literal: The ru scholars greatly took it as glory.
idiomatic: The ru scholars greatly took it as glory.

literal: When Chuo was made grand marshal, Linghui as prince's teacher concurrently held the post of chief of staff in the grand marshal's establishment office.
idiomatic: When Chuo was made grand marshal, Linghui as prince's teacher concurrently held the post of chief of staff in the grand marshal's establishment office.

literal: When Chuo was executed, Linghui was suspended and dismissed.
idiomatic: When Chuo was executed, Linghui was suspended and dismissed.

literal: After Chuo's death, on each seventh day and at the end of the hundredth day Linghui always begged monks on Chuo's behalf and set out offerings, turning the sutras and walking the rite.
idiomatic: After Chuo's death, on each seventh day and at the end of the hundredth day Linghui always begged monks on Chuo's behalf and set out offerings, turning the sutras and walking the rite.

literal: Several years after Qi's fall he died.
idiomatic: Several years after Qi's fall he died.

literal: His son Wanshou was clever, perceptive, and quick; he ranged widely through many books, mastered the main purport of both Rites and Commentaries, had literary polish, and was especially given to poetry.
idiomatic: His son Wanshou was clever, perceptive, and quick; he ranged widely through many books, mastered the main purport of both Rites and Commentaries, had literary polish, and was especially given to poetry.

literal: Late in Qi, Yang Xiuzhi recruited him as traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government.
idiomatic: Late in Qi, Yang Xiuzhi recruited him as traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government.

literal: Under Sui he was court gentleman attendant, literary scholar to the Prince of Teng, and chief administrator of Yuzhang.
idiomatic: Under Sui he was court gentleman attendant, literary scholar to the Prince of Teng, and chief administrator of Yuzhang.

literal: He died in the post of direct judge in the Court of Review.
idiomatic: He died in the post of direct judge in the Court of Review.

literal: Ma Zijie—his forebears were men of Fufeng.
idiomatic: Ma Zijie—his forebears were men of Fufeng.

literal: For generations they dwelt in the Liang lands; in the Taihe era they entered Luoyang.
idiomatic: For generations they dwelt in the Liang lands; in the Taihe era they entered Luoyang.

literal: Father and grandfathers alike held clean offices.
idiomatic: Father and grandfathers alike held clean offices.

literal: The three brothers Zijie, Zilian, and Zishang were all versed in letters.
idiomatic: The three brothers Zijie, Zilian, and Zishang were all versed in letters.

literal: When Yang Xiuzhi governed West Yan, Zilian, Zishang, Zijie, and the other court gentlemen each had a poem of farewell; Yang gathered them into one piece in reply—that is the poem that says "the three Ma all have white brows."
idiomatic: When Yang Xiuzhi governed West Yan, Zilian, Zishang, Zijie, and the other court gentlemen each had a poem of farewell; Yang gathered them into one piece in reply—that is the poem that says "the three Ma all have white brows."

literal: Zijie was promoted from traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government to recorder for Prince of Nanyang Chuo and followed Chuo to Ding province.
idiomatic: Zijie was promoted from traveling staff officer in an establishment that opened the government to recorder for Prince of Nanyang Chuo and followed Chuo to Ding province.

literal: Whenever Chuo went out to tour and hunt, he always made Zijie run his horse alongside the game.
idiomatic: Whenever Chuo went out to tour and hunt, he always made Zijie run his horse alongside the game.

literal: Zijie was by nature ru-soft; his robes trailed and his hat slipped, and he would cry out or weep; Chuo had the riders drive him on and would not stop until Zijie fell from his horse—Chuo took it for sport.
idiomatic: Zijie was by nature ru-soft; his robes trailed and his hat slipped, and he would cry out or weep; Chuo had the riders drive him on and would not stop until Zijie fell from his horse—Chuo took it for sport.

literal: By this he gradually grew intimate; Chuo memorialized to make him consulting aide.
idiomatic: By this he gradually grew intimate; Chuo memorialized to make him consulting aide.

literal: Shi Yao, styled Baiyao, was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan; he too advanced through Confucian learning.
idiomatic: Shi Yao, styled Baiyao, came from Anxi in Zhongshan; he too advanced through Confucian learning.

literal: In office he reached the end as pure and frugal.
idiomatic: In office he reached the end as pure and frugal.

literal: In Wuping he was governor of Liyang commandery; it happened that Hulü Wudu went out as inspector of Yan province—Wudu was the heir of the Chancellor, Prince of Xianyang, and the empress's elder brother, and by nature was very greedy and violent.
idiomatic: In Wuping he was governor of Liyang commandery; it happened that Hulü Wudu went out as inspector of Yan province—Wudu was the heir of the Chancellor, Prince of Xianyang, and the empress's elder brother, and by nature was very greedy and violent.

literal: He had first passed through Wei county; the magistrate, assistant, and those below had levied several thousand bolts of silk as gifts to him.
idiomatic: He had first passed through Wei county; the magistrate, assistant, and those below had levied several thousand bolts of silk as gifts to him.

literal: When he reached Liyang he had those at his side hint and stir up Yao and the county officials under the commandery.
idiomatic: When he reached Liyang he had those at his side hint and stir up Yao and the county officials under the commandery.

literal: Yao held a single bolt of silk in his hand and said to Wudu: "This is old Shi's loom-cloth; I offer it merely as a gift.
idiomatic: Yao held a single bolt of silk in his hand and said to Wudu, "This is old Shi's loom-cloth; I offer it merely as a gift.

literal: Beyond this, everything must come from clerks and people; of what belongs to clerks and people, not a hair's breadth may be rashly touched."
idiomatic: Beyond this, everything must come from clerks and people; of what belongs to clerks and people, not a hair's breadth may be rashly touched."

literal: Wudu also knew Yao was pure, plain, and a pure ru; he laughed and did not blame him.
idiomatic: Wudu also knew Yao was pure, plain, and a pure ru; he laughed and did not blame him.

literal: He authored ten juan of Master Shi, whose words were very shallow and vulgar.
idiomatic: He authored ten juan of Master Shi, whose words were very shallow and vulgar.

literal: Later he ended his days as inspector of Qiao province.
idiomatic: Later he ended his days as inspector of Qiao province.

literal: Beyond this, their deeds in the histories are lacking.
idiomatic: Beyond this, their deeds in the histories are lacking.

literal: Praise: The Great Way has already been hidden; name and teaching are what one follows—with these a state is built, with these a person stands.
idiomatic: Praise: The Great Way has already been hidden; name and teaching are what one follows—with these a state is built, with these a person stands.

literal: The imperial design mixed with hegemony; the ru wind was not yet pure—how could it not fall? To keep it from falling was to enlarge it in men.
idiomatic: The imperial design mixed with hegemony; the ru wind was not yet pure—how could it not fall? To keep it from falling was to enlarge it in men.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
